findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove, leaving user_count counter cache and primary_group stale
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association removes the join rows with a `delete_all`, which skips ActiveRecord callbacks. `GroupUser` maintains `groups.user_count` through a counter cache / callbacks, and `Group#remove` additionally clears `users.primary_group_id` when the removed group was the user's primary group. By deleting the join rows directly, the group's `user_count` column is never decremented (so the admin group list and the new `{{user_count}}`/pagination UI show wrong totals forever) and a removed member can keep the deleted group as their primary group. The symmetric add path correctly uses `group.add(user)`; removal should use `group.remove(user)` (after looking the user up) so the same bookkeeping runs.

findings.title: create silently drops alias_level
findings.body: `create` only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`, but the client's `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` (used by both `create` and `save`) always sends `alias_level`, and the admin form lets you pick an alias level before the first save. As a result a newly created group is always persisted with the default alias level and the user's selection is lost without any error; it only takes effect if they save a second time (where `update` does honour `alias_level`). `create` should assign `alias_level` the same way `update` does.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit/offset in public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()` on this unauthenticated-reachable endpoint. A negative value (e.g. `/groups/foo/members.json?offset=-1` or `limit=-1`) makes PostgreSQL raise "OFFSET must not be negative" / "LIMIT must not be negative", turning user input into a 500, and an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `limit=1000000`) forces the server to load and serialize every member of a large group, which is an easy resource-exhaustion vector. Clamp both values (e.g. offset >= 0, limit between 1 and a sane maximum).

findings.title: Breaking change to /groups/:name/members.json response shape and default truncation
findings.body: The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized members (and only paginated automatic groups). It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and applies a default `limit` of 50 to every group. Any existing consumer (plugins, mobile clients, scripts) that iterates the top-level array will break, and callers that relied on getting the whole membership now silently receive at most 50 users. This needs at least a changelog/version note, and ideally the pagination default should be documented; consider whether the old array shape must be preserved for compatibility.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups instead of a promise
findings.body: The early return was changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`, so `findMembers()` now returns `undefined` when the group has no name (the "new group" case in the admin UI). Any caller that chains on the result — e.g. `group.findMembers().then(...)`, or the controller's `next`/`previous` actions whose return value is used by the Ember action/promise machinery — will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. Return a resolved promise instead.

findings.title: totalPages off by one produces an extra empty page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 150 members with limit 50) this yields 4 instead of 3. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the "next" arrow stays enabled on the real last page, advancing `offset` to 150 and rendering an empty member list labelled page 4/4. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: addMembers/removeMember ignore server errors
findings.body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` fire `model.addMembers(...)` / `model.removeMember(...)` without attaching a rejection handler. The server returns 422 for automatic groups and can also fail for other reasons, and unknown usernames are silently skipped by `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`. The admin therefore gets no feedback at all: the input keeps its content (see the "TODO: should clear the input"), the list is not refreshed, and nothing indicates the operation failed. Add a failure handler that surfaces the error message (as the `save` action already does).

findings.title: add_members raises NoMethodError when usernames is sent as an array
findings.body: `usernames.split(",")` assumes the parameter is a String. An API client (or a nested form encoding such as `usernames[]=bob`) yields an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, producing an unhandled NoMethodError / 500 instead of a 400-class response. Coerce with `Array(params[:usernames]).join(',').split(',')` or validate the type explicitly.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route only accepts DELETE
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` maps only `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs bypass verb-based route recognition, so the test passes while exercising a request that cannot actually be made against the app; a regression in the route verb would go unnoticed. Use `xhr :delete` as the other remove_member example does.

findings.title: Lost coverage for unknown/non-member usernames and no coverage for the new members pagination
findings.body: The old specs asserted that adding a non-existent username and removing a non-member succeed silently; those cases are dropped here even though `add_members` still swallows unknown usernames, so that behaviour is now untested. Additionally, `GroupsController#members` was rewritten (new `{members:, meta:}` envelope, new default limit, new offset handling) without any spec update, so the response shape and the limit/offset edge cases are entirely uncovered.
